mappings.note: Grafting is the method (LO-7), but the question asked is whose genetic characteristics the fruit expresses, which is the heredity twin LO-9. Both twins are used because the item genuinely has both halves; a grafting item that only asked for the procedure takes LO-7 alone.
Identifies which organ of Bryophyllum does the propagating. Pure method identification, so the C3.2 twin; the genetic consequence is stated in the answer but never asked, so not LO-9.

Spore formation as an asexual mode, read off a conditions table. LO-7 is the frame's only asexual-reproduction outcome. Weak fit in that the item actually tests germination conditions, which no outcome covers.

POOR FIT. Asks the planting angle for a stem cutting, a horticultural procedure detail. No outcome in the frame descends to technique; LO-7 is cited because cutting is a method of asexual reproduction, which is the only hook available.
Which two plant parts grafting combines. Method identification, so the C3.2 twin, not LO-9; nothing genetic is asked, unlike the sibling grafting item about which plant the fruit resembles.

Tissue culture as a propagation method and its virus-free advantage. LO-12 deliberately NOT cited: it names Maheshwari and Indian tissue-culture research, and this item mentions neither, so citing it would map the chapter's topic rather than the question.

The student must read a labelled pistil diagram, which is what C-5.1-LO-1 (illustrate the structure of reproductive units) uniquely covers, then identify the site of fertilisation (C-3.2-LO-4). Verbal sibling items on the same content take LO-8 instead of C-5.1-LO-1.

Recognising budding in yeast from a microscope observation. Method identification under the C3.2 twin; the distractors rule out fusion of cells, so the asexual/sexual distinction is what is being tested.

Names the structure responsible for asexual reproduction in Rhizopus. Same outcome as the other spore items, distinguished from them only by which sub-fact is recalled; this family honestly shares one outcome.
Asks for the genetic consequence of mitosis (clones). The heredity twin, not LO-7, because no method is being named or compared as a process.

Refrigeration slows spore reproduction. Applied asexual-reproduction biology; LO-7 is the only outcome that reaches spore formation. Weak: the item is really about food preservation, which the frame does not cover.

The table is stamen and pistil presence, so LO-8 (male and female reproductive organs in plants) is what the student must know; C-3.2-LO-4 for the inference about which species can self-pollinate. Not C-5.1-LO-1: this is a table, not a structure to illustrate.

POOR FIT. Chronological ordering of the layering procedure. Like the cutting-angle item, this is horticultural technique with no outcome behind it; LO-7 is the nearest hook because layering is asexual propagation.

POOR FIT. Louis Pasteur and biogenesis. The scientist-attribution shape of this item looks like C6.1/LO-11/LO-12, but Pasteur is not an Indian contribution, so those are wrong; and the frame has no outcome for germ theory or life from pre-existing life. Competency only.
Why clonal offspring fare badly when the environment changes. The reasoning is absence of genetic variation, so the C3.3-parented twin, matching the sibling item on vegetatively propagated crops.

Answered by reading labels M, N, O off a diagram of the female system, which is C-5.1-LO-1; LO-8 for knowing which organ produces gametes and which receives the embryo. The diagram is what separates this from the verbal oviduct item, which takes LO-8 alone.

Why chromosome number does not double each generation. This is constancy, not variation, so C-3.3-LO-5 does not apply; the frame has no meiosis outcome, so the mechanism-of-heredity competency is the honest ceiling.

46 to 23 in gametes. Same gap as the other meiosis items: chromosome arithmetic has no learning outcome in this frame. Distinguished from its siblings only by being the recall form rather than the reasoning form.

Names the outermost whorl (sepal). LO-8 is deliberately NOT used: sepals are neither the male nor the female reproductive organ, so LO-8's text does not reach them. C-5.1-LO-1 covers the structure of the flower as the plant's reproductive unit, which does.

Pure trait-to-agent matching: which listed features belong to insect-pollinated plants. C-2.8-LO-1 is withheld here, unlike the night-flower and apple-orchard items, because no interaction or consequence is examined, only the adaptation list.
Matches stamen, pistil, anther and ovary to their descriptions. Textbook LO-8. Not C-5.1-LO-1: no diagram or illustration is involved, which is the rule used throughout this chapter to split the two.

The purpose of emasculating and bagging a pea bud is to control pollination. Same outcome as the other bagging items; what varies across that family is only whether the student must name the technique, order its steps, or predict its result.
Straight definitional contrast of self and cross pollination. LO-4 without C-4.3-LO-1, because the correct option is about where the pollen goes, not which agent carries it.
Ovary to fruit, ovule to seed. This is the one outcome in the frame written for exactly this fact, and the only item family that uses it cleanly with nothing else attached.

POOR FIT. Identifies ovulation as the day-14 event on a cycle chart. The frame has no ovulation or menstrual-cycle outcome. Not LO-8, because the item asks for a process, not for the ovary as an organ.
